crew.overview: A story about a troubled boy growing up in England, set in 1983. He comes across a few skinheads on his way home from school, after a fight. They become his new best friends, even like family. Based on experiences of director Shane Meadows.
crew.title: This Is England

crew.overview: A soldier returns to his small town and exacts a deadly revenge on the thugs who tormented his disabled brother while he was away.
crew.title: Dead Man's Shoes

crew.overview: A young farmer in rural Yorkshire numbs his daily frustrations with binge drinking and casual sex, until the arrival of a Romanian migrant worker.
crew.title: God's Own Country

crew.overview: In 1840s England, palaeontologist Mary Anning and a young woman sent by her husband to convalesce by the sea develop an intense relationship. Despite the chasm between their social spheres and personalities, Mary and Charlotte discover they can each offer what the other has been searching for: the realisation that they are not alone. It is the beginning of a passionate and all-consuming love affair that will defy all social bounds and alter the course of both lives irrevocably.
crew.title: Ammonite

details.biography:
Chris Wyatt has worked with an eclectic mix of acclaimed British film directors from Peter Greenaway to Shane Meadows. Spanning a career of more than forty years, credits include The Pillow Book; This is England and Dreams of a Life. Chris has been nominated twice for a BIFA craft award for Dead Man’s Shoes and ’71 which followed a long and continuing association with director Yann Demange.

Chris has just completed God’s Own Country with writer/director Francis Lee, backed by the BFI and Creative England it will premiere in competition at Sundance 2017.
details.name: Chris Wyatt
